                    ### Question
                    A 57-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes mellitus comes to the physician for a follow-up examination. She previously had been compliant with her diet and medication but has had a 5-kg (11-lb) weight gain since the last visit 6 months ago. She reports that she often misses doses of her metformin. Her hemoglobin A1c is 9.8%. Which of the following is the most appropriate course of action?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Refer the patient to a dietician
opb. Schedule more frequent follow-up visits
opc. Refer the patient to an endocrinologist
opd. Add glyburide to the medication regimen
ope. Stop metformin and begin an insulin regimen

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient's poor medication adherence, resulting in a high hemoglobin A1c of 9.8%, weight gain, and possible insulin resistance, suggests a need for treatment intensification. Considering the reduced efficacy of metformin due to non-adherence, adding glyburide or transitioning to an insulin regimen may be appropriate. Referral to an endocrinologist for further management could also be beneficial.
